note: Catalogue of the gaming launchers Lindos can install. Used by `lindos-game` (list/status/install/launch) and by Lindos Settings → Gaming. `id` values are exactly the items accepted by /usr/libexec/lindos/install-gaming.sh and by the helper action install-gaming ({"items": [...]}). `check` is evaluated in order dpkg → flatpak → which. Honesty: Wine/Proton are translation layers, not Windows; Sober is a community Roblox runtime (not the Windows client); mcpelauncher is unofficial; whether a Steam game runs online depends on its anti-cheat (see compat-matrix.json).

launchers.name: Steam
launchers.description: Valve's store and launcher. Windows games run through Proton (Steam Play); enable it for all titles in Settings → Compatibility.
launchers.note: Multiplayer titles only work when the developer enabled their anti-cheat for Proton — check areweanticheatyet.com and protondb.com. Some (Apex Legends, Rust, Destiny 2, Call of Duty and others) are not supported on Lindos yet: that is up to their publishers.

launchers.name: Lutris
launchers.description: Open-source game manager: Battle.net, EA app, Ubisoft Connect, GOG, Amazon, emulators and any Windows installer, with Wine/Proton runners.
launchers.note: Ubuntu 'universe' ships Lutris 0.5.x; falls back to the Flathub package.

launchers.name: Heroic Games Launcher
launchers.description: Epic Games Store, GOG and Amazon Prime Gaming library — Windows titles run through Proton/Wine.
launchers.note: Fortnite is not supported on Lindos yet: Epic keeps Easy Anti-Cheat for Linux disabled, and whether that changes is up to Epic, its publisher. Other Epic titles generally work.

launchers.name: Prism Launcher
launchers.description: Minecraft Java Edition launcher (native Linux) with instances, mod loaders and bundled Java runtimes. Requires a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft.
launchers.note: Java edition only. Bedrock is a separate, unofficial launcher (mcpelauncher).

launchers.name: Roblox (Sober)
launchers.description: Roblox through Sober — a community Linux runtime for the Android build. Roblox's own Windows client does not run on Linux (Hyperion anti-cheat).
launchers.note: Not affiliated with Roblox Corporation. Works with the normal Roblox account; some experiences that need Windows-only features may differ.

launchers.name: Roblox Studio (Vinegar)
launchers.description: Roblox Studio (the game editor) through Vinegar, which manages a Wine prefix for the Windows Studio build.
launchers.note: Studio only — Vinegar no longer runs the Roblox player; use Sober for playing.

launchers.name: Minecraft Bedrock (mcpelauncher)
launchers.description: Unofficial launcher that runs the Android build of Minecraft Bedrock Edition. You must own Minecraft on Google Play and sign in with that account.
launchers.note: Not affiliated with Mojang/Microsoft; marketplace and Realms may not work; treat as 'partial'.

launchers.name: Bottles
launchers.description: Friendly manager for Wine prefixes ('bottles') with per-app runners, DXVK/VKD3D and dependency installers — used by the Lindos Creator recipes.
launchers.note: Wine is a compatibility layer, not Windows: recent Adobe releases and apps with kernel drivers/anti-cheat do not work.
